stories.headline: Amazon's Custom Chip Business Hits $20B+ Run Rate; Jassy Floats Selling Chips to Third Parties

key_facts.fact: Amazon's custom chip business — Graviton CPUs, Trainium AI chips, and Nitro networking cards — now has an annualized revenue run rate of over $20 billion, doubling from $10B disclosed with Q4 results.
Jassy said if the chip unit operated as a standalone business selling to third parties, it could achieve an annual run rate of around $50 billion.
Jassy wrote 'There's so much demand for our chips that it's quite possible we'll sell racks of them to third parties in the future.'
AWS's AI business is running at over $15 billion in annualized revenue as of Q1 2026, the first time Amazon has reported the figure.
Trainium2 is fully allocated, Trainium3 (reaching customers early 2026) has nearly all supply reserved, and Trainium4 already has substantial pre-orders.
Amazon projects roughly $200 billion in capital expenditure in 2026, mainly focused on AI infrastructure.
Jassy said using Trainium at scale would 'save tens of billions of capex dollars per year, and provide several hundred basis points of operating margin advantage versus relying on others' chips.'

stories.headline: Jassy Says AWS AI Revenue Hits $15B Run Rate, Amazon Custom Chips Now at $20B+

key_facts.fact: AWS's AI revenue run rate has reached over $15 billion as of Q1 2026, up from essentially nothing three years ago, according to Andy Jassy's annual shareholder letter.

Amazon's three custom silicon lines — Graviton, Trainium, and Nitro — produce over $20 billion in annualized revenue, growing at triple-digit rates YoY; Jassy estimates the business would be worth ~$50 billion if sold externally.

Amazon plans to spend approximately $200 billion in capital expenditures in 2026, primarily on AI infrastructure; Jassy wrote 'We're not investing approximately $200 billion in capex in 2026 on a hunch.'

Jassy said using Trainium at scale will 'save tens of billions of capex dollars per year, and provide several hundred basis points of operating margin advantage versus relying on others' chips for inference.'
Amazon's total revenue grew 12% YoY to $717 billion in 2025 with $80 billion operating income, but free cash flow fell from $38 billion to $11 billion due to heavy AI infrastructure spending.
Jassy pointed to a deal with OpenAI worth more than $100 billion as a signal of AI demand backing Amazon's spending plans.

stories.headline: Anthropic Weighs Designing Its Own AI Chips as Revenue Surpasses $30B Annualized

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is exploring the possibility of designing its own chips, according to three sources, though plans are in preliminary stages and the company could still opt to only purchase chips.
The company has yet to commit to a specific design or assemble a dedicated team for chip development.
Anthropic currently trains and runs Claude using a mix of AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, and Nvidia GPUs.
Anthropic's annualized revenue now exceeds $30 billion, up from around $9 billion at the end of 2025.
Broadcom has signed a deal to provide Anthropic with access to around 3.5 gigawatts of AI computing capacity using Google's processors starting in 2027.

stories.headline: NASA's Artemis 2 Crew Set for Pacific Splashdown Tonight After Historic Moon Flyby

key_facts.fact: The Artemis 2 crew — astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and CSA's Jeremy Hansen — is scheduled to splash down off the coast of San Diego at approximately 8:07 PM EDT on Friday, April 10.
Artemis 2 is NASA's first crewed mission to the moon since Apollo 17 in 1972; the crew swung around the far side of the Moon on April 6 and exited the lunar sphere of influence on April 7.

Orion will perform a 'lofted' reentry — dipping into the atmosphere, skipping up, then descending again — to reduce heat stress on the heat shield after unexpected char losses during the uncrewed Artemis 1 mission.
The service module will separate around 7:33 PM EDT, parachutes deploy at 8:04 PM, with USS John P. Murtha recovery operations within two hours of splashdown.
NASA Associate Administrator Amit Kshatriya said: 'To every engineer, every technician that's touched this machine tomorrow belongs to you. The crew has done their part. Now we have to do ours.'

stories.headline: Bessent and Powell Summon Wall Street CEOs to Warn About Anthropic Mythos Cyber Risks

key_facts.fact: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Fed Chair Jerome Powell summoned CEOs of systemically important banks to an urgent meeting at Treasury headquarters to discuss cyber risks from Anthropic's Mythos model.
Mythos can identify and exploit vulnerabilities in every major operating system and web browser when directed by a user, according to Anthropic's own disclosures.
CEOs summoned include Citigroup's Jane Fraser, Morgan Stanley's Ted Pick, Bank of America's Brian Moynihan, Wells Fargo's Charlie Scharf, and Goldman Sachs's David Solomon.
Anthropic limited Mythos release to about 40 major tech and finance firms under 'Project Glasswing,' including Amazon, Apple, and JPMorgan, to secure critical systems before broader availability.
Anthropic had been in discussions with US officials about Mythos's 'offensive and defensive cyber capabilities' prior to its release.

stories.headline: Anthropic Makes Claude Cowork Generally Available With Enterprise Controls and Zoom Integration

key_facts.fact: Claude Cowork, previously a research preview, is now generally available to all paid Anthropic plans (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise) on macOS and Windows.
Six enterprise features were added: role-based access controls, group spend limits, usage analytics, expanded OpenTelemetry support, a Zoom MCP connector, and per-tool connector controls.

Claude Cowork uses the same agentic architecture that powers Claude Code, enabling complex multi-step tasks with direct local file access and sub-agent coordination, now without requiring the terminal.
Anthropic launched Cowork as a research preview 12 weeks ago; since then millions have adopted it and hundreds of thousands more try it weekly, according to Felix Rieseberg at Anthropic.
PayPal is among early enterprise adopters rolling out Cowork across teams, with a joint webinar planned for April 16 on deployment best practices.

stories.headline: Eli Lilly's Foundayo, First Oral GLP-1 Weight-Loss Pill, Now Available in the US at $149/Month

key_facts.fact: Eli Lilly announced on April 9 that Foundayo (orforglipron), the only oral GLP-1 pill approved for weight loss, is now available in the US via LillyDirect, telehealth providers, and retail pharmacies.
Foundayo starts at $149/month for self-pay patients; commercially insured patients may pay as low as $25/month; Medicare Part D patients will pay $50/month starting July 1, 2026.
In the ATTAIN-1 trial, participants on the highest dose lost an average of 27.3 pounds (12.4%) vs. 2.2 pounds (0.9%) for placebo; the study enrolled 3,127 participants from 10 countries.
Foundayo is a once-daily pill with no food or water restrictions, a key differentiator from injectable GLP-1 treatments like Lilly's own Zepbound (tirzepatide). FDA approved it on April 1, 2026.
Orforglipron was originally discovered by Chugai Pharmaceutical and licensed to Lilly in 2018. The ATTAIN clinical program enrolled more than 4,500 participants across two global trials.

stories.headline: Florida Attorney General Launches Investigation Into OpenAI Over FSU Shooting and Child Safety

key_facts.fact: Florida AG James Uthmeier launched an investigation into OpenAI and ChatGPT, citing national security concerns, alleged links to criminal behavior, and ChatGPT's role in the April 2025 Florida State University mass shooting that killed two.
Uthmeier said subpoenas to OpenAI are 'forthcoming' and raised concerns about OpenAI's data falling 'into the hands of America's enemies, such as the Chinese Communist Party.'
OpenAI said it will cooperate, noting ChatGPT has over 900 million weekly active users and the company builds it 'to understand people's intent and respond in a safe and appropriate way.'
The probe comes as OpenAI prepares for an IPO that could value it at up to $1 trillion.
The family of shooting victim Robert Morales plans to sue OpenAI; attorneys claim the shooter 'was in constant communication' with ChatGPT leading up to the attack.

stories.headline: Google and Intel Expand Multiyear Deal on Xeon CPUs and Custom ASIC-Based IPUs for AI

key_facts.fact: Intel and Google announced a multiyear collaboration to deploy multiple generations of Intel Xeon processors (including Xeon 6) across Google Cloud and to co-develop next-generation custom ASIC-based IPUs.
Intel's custom ASIC business grew more than 50% in 2025 and exited Q4 at an annualized revenue run rate above $1 billion, per Intel CFO David Zinsner.

The IPUs offload networking, security, and storage operations from host CPUs, freeing resources for AI tenant workloads — similar in concept to Amazon's Nitro NICs and Microsoft's FPGA-based approach.
Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan stated: 'Scaling AI requires more than accelerators — it requires balanced systems.'
Google's Amin Vahdat, SVP and Chief Technologist of AI Infrastructure, called Intel a 'trusted partner for nearly two decades' and said its Xeon road map gives confidence to meet growing AI demands.

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches $100/Month ChatGPT Pro Tier as Codex Hits 3 Million Weekly Users

key_facts.fact: OpenAI introduced a new $100/month ChatGPT Pro subscription tier positioned between the $20 Plus plan and the existing $200 Pro plan, focused on heavier Codex usage.
The new tier offers 5x more Codex usage than Plus, with a temporary promotional boost to 10x through May 31, 2026.
Codex now has over 3 million weekly users, growing 5x in three months with around 70% month-on-month growth.
OpenAI is simultaneously 'rebalancing' Codex usage in the $20 Plus plan to support more sessions across the week rather than longer single-day sessions.
Pro subscribers get access to GPT-5.4 Pro for advanced reasoning, unlimited GPT-5.3 usage, faster image generation, and expanded capabilities for agent-style tasks.

stories.headline: Chinese AI Firm Sharetronic Disclosed $92M in Banned Nvidia Chip Servers After Super Micro Charges

key_facts.fact: Shenzhen-based Sharetronic Data Technology's stock plunged 20% (daily limit) hours after the US charged Super Micro Computer co-founder with smuggling billions in Nvidia chips to China.

Records filed with Chinese government agencies show Sharetronic procured hundreds of Super Micro systems containing banned Nvidia H100 and H200 chips worth approximately $92 million (6.32 billion yuan).
Bloomberg found 17 invoices in China's national tax database totaling approximately 60 billion yuan, representing only about one-fifth of Sharetronic's planned total procurement.
Sharetronic's subsidiary FCloud, established in 2024, became one of only 8 certified Nvidia Cloud Partners in China and announced plans to procure 32.2 billion yuan in hardware.
Nvidia, Super Micro, and Dell all denied having sales relationships with Sharetronic, which also denied any business cooperation with Super Micro — contradicting the invoice records.

Super Micro co-founder was charged by the DOJ with helping transfer approximately $2.5 billion in Nvidia servers to China; smuggling methods included forged export documents and shell servers in warehouses.

stories.headline: RISC-V Chip Designer SiFive Raises $400M Series G at $3.65B Valuation, Eyes IPO

key_facts.fact: SiFive raised $400 million in an oversubscribed Series G round led by Atreides Management, with participation from Apollo, Nvidia, Point72 Turion, and T. Rowe Price.
The financing values SiFive at $3.65 billion and CEO Patrick Little said he expects it to be the firm's last private round before filing for a public offering.
SiFive sells customizable RISC-V processor IP — not chips — that customers like Google can use for their own internal chip designs, competing with Arm Holdings.
Arm's recent move to develop its own chips created an opening for SiFive, as Arm became a potential competitor to its longtime customers.
SiFive will use the funding to develop a data center CPU design and expand global engineering teams, with existing ports of CUDA, RedHat, and Ubuntu on its platform.

stories.headline: TSMC Q1 Revenue Surges 35% to $35.7B, Beating Estimates as AI Chip Demand Holds

key_facts.fact: TSMC reported January-March 2026 revenue of T$1.134 trillion ($35.71 billion), up 35% year-over-year from T$839.3 billion, beating the LSEG SmartEstimate of T$1.125 trillion from 20 analysts.
The result was in line with TSMC's own January guidance of $34.6 billion to $35.8 billion, signaling AI chip demand remained intact despite the Middle East war disrupting energy costs.
Analysts raised their forecast for TSMC's April-June revenue by 2.3% over the last 30 days to a record T$1.2 trillion, betting on constrained capacity for advanced AI chip production.
TSMC's Taipei-listed shares have gained 29% year-to-date versus 22% for the benchmark index. The company will report full Q1 earnings on April 16.
TSMC raised its 2026 capex budget to $52–56 billion (up ~30% from $40.9B in 2025), primarily for 3nm and 2nm node expansion. Its 2nm capacity is already fully booked for 2026 by Apple and Nvidia.

stories.headline: Unitree to Launch $4,370 Humanoid Robot R1 Globally via AliExpress Next Week

key_facts.fact: Unitree Robotics will launch its cheapest humanoid robot, the R1, in international markets next week via Alibaba's AliExpress platform, according to two sources familiar with the matter.
The R1 is priced at 29,900 yuan (~$4,370) in China, making it one of the most affordable humanoid robots on the market. Overseas pricing has not been announced.
The launch will cover North America, Europe, Japan, and Singapore, with additional channels to follow later.
The R1 stands 123cm tall, weighs at least 27kg, has 26 joints, and can perform cartwheels, run downhill, lie down and stand up unassisted.
The R1 will be available through Alibaba's Brand+ channel on AliExpress, the curated storefront for globally recognized brands.

stories.headline: US-Iran Ceasefire Frays as Hormuz Stays Blocked; Israel Agrees to Direct Lebanon Talks

key_facts.fact: In the first 24 hours of the ceasefire, just a single oil products tanker and five dry bulk carriers passed through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries 140 ships and a fifth of the world's oil daily.
US-Iran talks are scheduled for Saturday April 11 in Islamabad, with Vice President JD Vance leading the US delegation opposite Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf.
Israeli PM Netanyahu said he has given instructions to start direct peace negotiations with Lebanon, with talks expected in Washington next week, focused on disarming Hezbollah.

Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei vowed retribution on the 40th day of mourning for his father, killed in US-Israeli airstrikes: 'We will certainly not leave unpunished the criminal aggressors.'

Trump said Iran was doing a 'very poor job' of allowing oil through the strait, while Iran cited Israel's ongoing Lebanon strikes — which killed over 250 on April 8 — as justification for keeping Hormuz blocked.
Three diplomats confirmed China used its leverage as Iran's biggest oil buyer to urge Tehran back to the negotiating table, with Trump acknowledging China played a role in the ceasefire.
The UAE intercepted 17 ballistic missiles and 45 drone attacks since the ceasefire began, while Kuwait reported intense attacks on oil infrastructure and three power/water desalination facilities.

stories.headline: xAI Sues Colorado to Block AI Anti-Discrimination Law, Citing First Amendment Violations

key_facts.fact: xAI filed a federal lawsuit against Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser to block enforcement of a 2024 state law requiring 'high-risk' AI system developers to protect consumers against 'algorithmic discrimination' in education, employment, housing, and other sectors.

xAI argues the law violates the First Amendment by prohibiting AI developers from 'producing speech that the State of Colorado dislikes' and compelling them to 'conform their speech to a State-enforced orthodoxy on controversial topics.'
Colorado was the first U.S. state to pass a comprehensive AI regulation bill; Governor Jared Polis signed it 'with reservations' and the law was delayed from February to June 30 to take effect.
xAI is seeking a court injunction to halt enforcement plus a formal declaration that the legislation is unconstitutional.

The lawsuit comes amid a broader fight between states drafting AI rules and the Trump administration pushing for a single federal framework, with Trump writing on Truth Social: 'There must be only One Rulebook if we are going to continue to lead in AI.'
